comparison.objective: PR-771 statically clamps two aligned boards with a one-hand bar clamp; the candidate commissions a shock absorber by adjusting, locking, and testing dynamic stopping behavior.
comparison.physical_skill: Both involve bimanual stabilization and force-controlled retention, but PR-771 positions clamp jaws and closes a ratchet, whereas the candidate requires recessed hex-key engagement, captive setscrew loosening/re-engagement, fine collar rotation, relocking, and response-guided iteration.
comparison.success_condition: PR-771 requires at least 20 N clamping force, sub-0.5 mm jaw gaps, board alignment, and a released clamp held for 1 s. The candidate instead requires two physical impact cycles at ≥0.85 J and 0.3–3.30 m/s without exceeding 12 mm stroke, striking the hard stop, overloading, excessive rebound, or drifting after locking. Candidate rebound, overload, drift, and witness-torque thresholds remain undeclared.
comparison.reason: Static workpiece clamping and dynamic energy-absorption commissioning test meaningfully different abilities and outcomes; shared counterholding and force control are generic primitives.
